<description>
`sign_ecdsa(..., rfc6979=True)` in the test framework derives the nonce from the raw message hash. RFC6979 section 2.3.4 (bits2octets) reduces the hash mod n first. libsecp256k1 has done so since 0.2.0. So for a hash >= n the framework's signature differs from libsecp256k1's, though it is still valid.

This is a small, correct fix with a test. The test checks two signatures computed with libsecp256k1, one of them for a hash >= n, and fails without the fix. The change has no practical effect on current tests: the only caller, `feature_taproot.py`, signs double-SHA256 sighashes, which are >= n with probability about 2^-128. If reviewers see no benefit, feel free to close it.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
bb96838c9d test: reduce hash mod n for RFC6979 nonce

RFC6979 section 2.3.4 (bits2octets) reduces the message hash modulo the
group order before it enters the nonce derivation. libsecp256k1 has
done so since 0.2.0. The test framework used the raw hash, so for a
hash >= n its deterministic signature differed from libsecp256k1's.

Add a test with signatures computed by libsecp256k1, one of them for a
hash >= n.
</commits>

diff --git a/test/functional/test_framework/key.py b/test/functional/test_framework/key.py
index 40c76e29fa..18ba3aa100 100644
--- a/test/functional/test_framework/key.py
+++ b/test/functional/test_framework/key.py
@@ -173,7 +173,8 @@ class ECKey:
         z = int.from_bytes(msg, 'big')
         # Note: no RFC6979 by default, but a simple random nonce (some tests rely on distinct transactions for the same operation)
         if rfc6979:
-            k = int.from_bytes(rfc6979_nonce(self.secret.to_bytes(32, 'big') + msg), 'big')
+            # RFC6979 section 2.3.4 (bits2octets): the hash is reduced mod n.
+            k = int.from_bytes(rfc6979_nonce(self.secret.to_bytes(32, 'big') + (z % ORDER).to_bytes(32, 'big')), 'big')
         else:
             k = random.randrange(1, ORDER)
         R = k * secp256k1.G
@@ -321,6 +322,18 @@ class TestFrameworkKey(unittest.TestCase):
         for sig in [b'', b'\x30', b'\x30\x00', b'\x30\x01\x02']:
             self.assertFalse(pubkey.verify_ecdsa(sig, msg))
 
+    def test_ecdsa_rfc6979(self):
+        """RFC6979 signatures match libsecp256k1, including for a hash >= n."""
+        privkey = ECKey()
+        privkey.set((1).to_bytes(32, 'big'), compressed=True)
+        vectors = [
+            (hashlib.sha256(b"Satoshi Nakamoto").digest(), "3045022100934b1ea10a4b3c1757e2b0c017d0b6143ce3c9a7e6a4a49860d7a6ab210ee3d802202442ce9d2b916064108014783e923ec36b49743e2ffa1c4496f01a512aafd9e5"),
+            # bits2octets reduces the hash mod n before deriving the nonce
+            ((ORDER + 1).to_bytes(32, 'big'), "304402206673ffad2147741f04772b6f921f0ba6af0c1e77fc439e65c36dedf4092e889802204c1a971652e0ada880120ef8025e709fff2080c4a39aae068d12eed009b68c89"),
+        ]
+        for msg, sig_hex in vectors:
+            self.assertEqual(privkey.sign_ecdsa(msg, rfc6979=True).hex(), sig_hex)
+
